clue.text: Prevent Chopin initially plugging one of his compositions?

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so the initial letter goes into the middle of the composition

parts.note: Chopin wrote many preludes for piano

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A puzzle about stopping one of Chopin's own piano pieces from being played.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to rule it out in advance, which is to prevent it.

clue.text: Stitch finally made runner fall

parts.note: purl is a knitting stitch

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: a river runs, so runner can stand for river, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A knitter's last stitch caused an athlete to trip.
explanation.walkthrough: A purler is British informal for a heavy headlong fall, as in 'come a purler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming a purler is a British informal phrase for taking a heavy headlong tumble.

clue.text: Docile pet initially not minding a walk in the park

parts.note: easy can mean placid, compliant

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: saying 'I'm easy' means you don't mind either way

explanation.surface: A well-behaved dog that doesn't mind being taken on its daily walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for something very simple, no effort at all.

clue.text: Erudite king with study facing north

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch

indicators.note: in a down clue, facing north means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: A wise monarch whose study faces north.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) means scholarly, having much knowledge.

clue.text: Daughter feeding magistrate's duck

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the daughter letter goes inside the magistrate's title

parts.note: a doge was chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa; the 's stands for 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A girl giving bread to a judge's pet duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' reads as a bird, but it is the verb meaning to avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to evade or sidestep it, as with a question or a blow.

clue.text: Fluid movement popular woman talked of

parts.note: something popular is said to be in

indicators.note: talked of says the woman's name is heard rather than written, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Flo is a woman's name, short for Florence

explanation.surface: Gossip about a well-liked woman, phrased like a note on liquids.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflow is a stream of liquid or gas coming in, a movement of fluid.

clue.text: Trivial old bird in northern lake

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the old bird goes between the northern and lake letters

parts.note: mina is a variant spelling of myna, the starling-like bird

explanation.surface: A minor sighting: an aged bird on a lake in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal sum or fee is a token, very small one, so trivial.

clue.text: Female councilLOR NAttering in the centre

indicators.note: in the centre says the letters sit in the middle of the words, where the capitals show them

explanation.surface: A woman councillor chatting away in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna is a woman's given name, made famous by the novel Lorna Doone.

clue.text: Foot-traveller means to get on river

parts.note: a way is a means or method
to fare is to get on, as in 'how did you fare?'

explanation.surface: A walker looks for a way of crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone travelling on foot, a walker on the road.

clue.text: Eccentric person's first-class pool

parts.note: crack means expert, top-class, as in 'crack troops'
a pot is a pool of money, as in a jackpot

explanation.surface: An odd individual's top-notch stake in the kitty.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is a crazy or eccentric person with odd ideas.

clue.text: Terribly sad, to marry and scorn an old county

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are in a dreadful state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable at having to wed a person and then spurn them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' between the fodder words is only a link. Ross and Cromarty was a county in the Scottish Highlands, abolished in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a former Scottish county, merged into Highland region in the 1970s.

clue.text: Former writer's ultimately excessive outlay

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former
a pen is a writing implement, so the writer's = pen's

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A one-time author's spending was, in the end, far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent on something, a cost or expenditure.

clue.text: Accountant keeping a set of books at work

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the accountant's letters surround the rest

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An accountant at the office holding onto a set of ledgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like the end of 'at work', but it is the definition: a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a musical composition for voices and instruments, so a work in the musical sense.

clue.text: Convenient-sounding cover for the Grand National for example

indicators.note: sounding says the word for convenient is heard, not spelt, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: handy means convenient
a cap is a covering, as for the head or a bottle

explanation.surface: Something that sounds useful covering the famous steeplechase.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase, run at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National is a handicap race: horses carry different weights to equalise their chances.

clue.text: Perverse artist in land without university

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the artist goes within the shortened land
without means lacking, so the university letter is dropped

parts.note: a country is a land or nation
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A wayward painter living somewhere with no university.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary (stressed on the second syllable) means stubbornly awkward, perverse.

clue.text: Source of light say backing sort of shelf

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters for say run in reverse

parts.note: e.g. means for example, i.e. say

explanation.surface: A lamp, for instance, fixed against the wall on some kind of shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow flat projection, like a shelf on a wall or a cliff.

clue.text: Day a surgeon flapped, posing risk

indicators.note: flapped means flustered or in a state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One day a surgeon panicked, putting the patient at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangerous carries a threat of harm, so it poses risk.

clue.text: Richly woven cloak originally worn by Catholic press chief

indicators.note: worn by means held inside, as clothing is by its wearer, so the cloak's letter goes within

parts.note: catholic (small c) means wide-ranging, i.e. broad

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: ED is an editor, head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A cardinal-like figure in a cloak, running a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' looks religious but means broad, as in catholic tastes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocaded fabric has raised patterns woven into it, often with gold or silver thread.

clue.text: Verse from sacred song mostly used in school class

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so the shortened song goes within the class letters

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter, so the song is cut short

parts.note: a hymn is a sacred song

explanation.surface: Poetry taken from a hymn and sung during a school lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme can mean verse or poetry in general, as in 'nursery rhyme'.

clue.text: Wake up in French quarter — outside as it happens

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the French and quarter letters go around the broadcast term

parts.note: en is French for in
N, north, is one quarter of the compass
a live broadcast goes out as events happen

explanation.surface: Coming round in a French district, outside, as events unfold.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven is to make livelier, rouse, wake up a gathering.

clue.text: Character by river absorbing current source of nourishment

parts.note: nu is a Greek letter, a character

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the river's letters surround the current symbol

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A figure by a river taking in the flow, looking for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance that provides nourishment to a living thing.

clue.text: Number in which vocalist misses start, holding note

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the shortened vocalist goes around the note
misses start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a singer is a vocalist
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A song in which the singer fluffs the opening but holds a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a song, but it is a mathematical number.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, with no fractional part.

clue.text: Strong man's woman, possibly, and male issue

parts.note: Sam can be a woman's name, short for Samantha, hence 'possibly'
a son is male offspring, issue

explanation.surface: The muscleman's partner, perhaps, and their baby boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Samson is the Biblical strongman whose power lay in his hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Samson, the Biblical hero of great strength, stands for any very strong man.

clue.text: Learner kept by Aussie mate, one getting down to work at last?

definitions.text: one getting down to work at last?

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the learner letter goes within the mate's word

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a friend
L is the learner sign

explanation.surface: A trainee taken in by an Australian friend, finally knuckling down to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block on which shoes are made, so 'at last' is a pun, not 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler mends shoes, working at a last, the shoe-shaped block.

clue.text: Spicy dish from US port? No more

indicators.note: no in front of the word more says those letters are to be left out

parts.note: Baltimore is a port city in Maryland

explanation.surface: A spicy dish from an American harbour city, now no longer available.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a curry cooked and served in a small wok-like pan, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Get boat refurbished in part of workshop

indicators.note: refurbished means done up, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Having a boat restored in one section of a workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part of' is link text; the definition is the single word 'workshop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottega is Italian for a shop or studio, especially an artist's workshop.

clue.text: Sound sort of tie a chap assumed at first for tea

indicators.note: assumed at first says the single letter a has taken on the chap at its front
sound says the tie word is heard, not spelt, giving its sound-alike

parts.note: a bow is a kind of tie, as in a bow tie
he is a male pronoun, a chap

explanation.surface: A healthy-looking bow tie that a man put on first, over tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a type of black China tea, once common in Britain.

clue.text: Do what's required, as distributors should

definitions.meaning: to fulfil one's promises or obligations, the idiomatic sense
distributors literally hand over merchandise to customers

explanation.surface: Distribution firms are expected to meet their obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fulfil expectations; literally it describes handing over merchandise, a distributor's job.

clue.text: Spirit served by club employee in part of UK

parts.note: a DJ plays records at a nightclub
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A drink poured by a nightclub worker somewhere in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' reads as a drink being served, but it is a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A djinni is a genie, a spirit of Arabian and Islamic folklore.

clue.text: Fish is available outside entrance to regimental HQ

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the fish and the rest go around the opening letter

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
on can mean available, as in 'on offer'

indicators.note: entrance to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Fish being served outside the entrance to the regiment's headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a military post where troops are stationed, serving as their base.
